html:
The expulsion of Germans from Czechoslovakia was the removal of about three million German speakers from the Czech lands in 1945 and 1946, after World War II, approved by the Allies at the Potsdam Conference.

Germans had lived in Bohemia and Moravia for some 700 years, mostly in the border Sudetenland. After the Munich Agreement and the Nazi occupation, the government of Edvard Beneš decided to expel them. In the first months there were violent wild expulsions and killings, such as at Ústí nad Labem and on the Brno death march. Later transports were organised. The Beneš decrees took their property. Thousands died, though numbers are disputed. Whole regions were resettled by Czechs. The expulsion was part of a wider expulsion of Germans from eastern Europe.
sum: The expulsion of Germans from Czechoslovakia was the removal of about three million German speakers from the Czech lands in 1945 and 1946, after World War II, approved by the Allies at the Potsdam Conference.
